question.text: For life insurance and investment-related insurance, what additional CDD must be conducted on beneficiaries?

answer.text: Obtain the full name including aliases of named beneficiaries, sufficient information for class beneficiaries, and determine if any beneficiary is a PEP
No additional CDD is required for beneficiaries of insurance policies
Only verify the beneficiary's identity at the time of policy purchase
Only screen beneficiaries against sanctions lists at the time of claim

explanation.text: The Logic: For life insurance and investment-related insurance, the RE must: (i) obtain full name including aliases of named natural person beneficiaries; (ii) for class beneficiaries (e.g., spouse, children), obtain sufficient information to identify them at payout time; and (iii) determine if beneficiaries or their beneficial owners are PEPs. Per the IFSCA workbook (p.102), these beneficiary measures are conducted as soon as the beneficiaries are identified or designated, with PEP determination at the latest at the time of payout. The Trap: Conduct beneficiary CDD as soon as beneficiaries are identified or designated, and determine PEP status at the latest at payout — it is not a "do it only at claim" or "do it only at inception" task. The senior-management escalation point applies only to higher-risk or PEP cases (p.103), not to every beneficiary. Note: Named-person beneficiaries require full name/aliases; class beneficiaries require sufficient information to identify at payout; PEP determination is mandatory at the latest at payout, with additional measures for higher-risk/PEP cases including senior-management approval before payout.
